title: What Protection Sold on a Car Rental Takes Off the Excess Borne
content:
What the protection sold on a hire takes off the excess the renter bears is read from that rental's own
ledger. This applies across the Car Rental Rate Classes.

| What the rental's ledger carries | Taken off the excess borne |
| --- | --- |
| both a collision damage waiver and theft protection sold on the rental | what was paid for both products |
| a collision damage waiver sold on the rental and no theft protection | what was paid for the waiver alone |
| neither | nothing |

Where the ledger carries both a collision damage waiver and theft protection sold on the rental, what was
paid for both products is taken off the excess borne. Where the ledger carries a collision damage waiver
sold on the rental and no theft protection, what was paid for the waiver alone is taken off the excess
borne. Where the ledger carries no collision damage waiver sold on the rental, nothing is taken off the
excess borne.

## What the deduction is measured on

The amount taken off is what was paid, not what the product is published at: it is the sum of the lines the
ledger carries for those products on that rental, however many days they were sold for.

Theft protection alone reaches no row. The first two rows both require a collision damage waiver standing on
the ledger, so a rental carrying theft protection without a waiver takes nothing off the excess borne.

## A four-day hire worked through

A rental whose ledger carries a collision damage waiver of 25.99 USD for each of 4 days, which is 103.96 USD,
and theft protection of 11.99 USD for each of those days, which is 47.96 USD: what is taken off the excess
borne is 151.92 USD. Where the same rental carries the waiver alone, 103.96 USD is taken off.
